extracted.intended_audience: general public / CNN readers interested in entertainment and LGBT issues
extracted.subtask_description: Norms and ethical expectations for stand-up comedy content and responses when a comedian's remarks harm audience members, especially regarding protected groups. Includes what counts as harmful material and appropriate remediation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stand-up comedy should 'heal people, not hurt'
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoted principle from the article: Morgan vowed to change his act to 'heal people, not hurt.' He apologized for 'bumming [the audience] out' and said he wants to 'change my message onstage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedic material should aim to bring people together or provide constructive insight rather than demean or wound audience members. Evaluate material by whether it attacks identities or contributes to harm vs. whether it fosters connection or insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hateful language targeting sexual orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm expressed in Morgan's apology: 'I don't have a hateful bone in my body' and 'I don't believe anyone should be bullied or made to feel bad about who they are.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use language that denigrates people for their sexual orientation or suggests that being gay is a negative or learned trait. Anti-patterns include labeling a group as inferior, suggesting changeability, or framing identity as a problem to be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not promote or joke about violence toward individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The article cites a reported line: 'if his own son told him he was gay, he would "pull out a knife and stab" him.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements that advocate, glorify, or joke about harming people cross a clear line; such violent rhetoric should be avoided. If an onstage remark includes threats or descriptions of violence, it will be judged as harmful even if intended as humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure onstage remarks are clearly framed as jokes, not rants
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience member's account: 'The sad thing is that none of this rant was a joke... His entire demeanor changed during that portion of the night. He was truly filled with some hate towards us.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comics should maintain comedic framing and delivery that signals intent to joke; when delivery shifts to a hostile rant, listeners interpret remarks as sincere and harmful. Evaluate tone, demeanor, and audience cues to distinguish humor from hateful ranting.

rubrics_metrics.name: When harm occurs, apologize directly and engage affected parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Morgan flew back to Nashville to deliver a face-to-face apology to people who were in the Ryman Auditorium and met with GLAAD and the Tennessee Equality Project; the gay audience member accepted the apology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate remediation after causing offense includes direct apologies to those harmed, meetings with community representatives, and listening to affected individuals. Face-to-face engagement is presented as an important step toward repair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take concrete corrective actions and public commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Morgan agreed to record a public service announcement for GLAAD's 'Amplify Your Voice' campaign and promised his future actions would be 'positive and supportive' of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond apology, public figures should commit to tangible follow-up (e.g., PSAs, working with advocacy organizations, changing material). Such commitments serve as evidence of accountability and intent to change behavior.
